reads.title: Israel’s Hind Rajab ‘investigation’ is a sham
reads.subtitle: Israel finally admits firing on her car. But don’t be fooled
reads.body:
- 933 days after five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab was killed alongside four of her cousins – all children – and their parents, Israel has finally admitted that its troops fired on the car carrying them.
This massacre goes beyond Hind and her family. Israel killed two paramedics sent to try to save her, after their ambulance’s journey had been coordinated with the Israeli authorities.
It comes after denial after denial, lie after lie, and fits a familiar pattern when Israel faces allegations over a particularly high-profile atrocity: deny, deflect, distort and sow doubt – and then, sometimes long after public attention has moved on, acknowledge facts that demolish the original story.
Most of the Western media plays along, refusing to assign responsibility even when overwhelming evidence warrants it. They instead encourage readers and viewers to retreat into a comforting shrug: who can possibly know what is real amid the fog of war?
So first let’s go through the truth and Israel’s lies – and then put it in the wider context of Israel’s record of relentless deception, and the culture of impunity which has enabled Israel’s Western-facilitated genocide against the Palestinian people.
If you subscribe, you can help us offer an alternative to the mainstream media

## What Israel has now admitted
On 19 August, the Israeli army announced that it had completed reviews of a number of what it calls “exceptional operational incidents” in Gaza.
It ordered Military Police criminal investigations into the killing of Hind Rajab and her family, and into the killing of 15 Palestinians – including emergency workers and a UN employee – in Tel al-Sultan in March 2025.
At the same time, it decided not to open a criminal investigation into the Israeli strikes which killed seven World Central Kitchen aid workers in April 2024. I’ll come back to that.
The Israeli military has stated that these reviews are conducted as part of its obligations under international law. Given the state’s wanton violations of international law, you might wonder about their motives for saying this.
It’s straightforward. In November 2024 the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant over war crimes and crimes against humanity. Under the ICC’s principle of complementarity, the Court is supposed to act where states with jurisdiction are unwilling or unable genuinely to investigate or prosecute the same conduct.
But simply announcing an investigation does not, by itself, block the ICC: the central question is whether domestic proceedings are genuine.
There is therefore an obvious legal and political incentive for Israel to point to investigations of a handful of high-profile cases as evidence that international intervention is unnecessary.
The record tells us there will be no meaningful accountability for Israel’s murder of Hind Rajab and her family.
Share

## What happened to Hind Rajab
On 29 January 2024, following Israeli evacuation orders – in practice, another episode of forced displacement – Hind’s aunt and uncle tried to flee Gaza City with Hind and her four cousins.
They were 15-year-old Layan Hamada, 13-year-old Raghad Hamada, 11-year-old Mohammed Hamada and seven-year-old Sara Hamada.
Israeli troops opened fire on their car. Five of its occupants were killed, leaving only Hind and Layan alive.
Layan called the Palestine Red Crescent. She said a tank was approaching and that her family had been killed. Gunfire can then be heard on the recording, followed by Layan screaming. The line went dead.
Hind was now the only survivor.
The Red Crescent re-established contact with her and spent around three and a half hours on the phone to a terrified five-year-old girl, wounded and trapped inside a car with the bodies of her family. As the day wore on, she spoke of her fear of the dark.
Eventually, an ambulance was dispatched after its movement had been coordinated with the Israeli authorities. The Red Crescent sent two paramedics: Yusuf al-Zeino, 35, and Ahmed al-Madhoun, 37.
As the ambulance reached the area, it was struck and both men were killed. Subsequent examinations of the wreckage found damage consistent with a tank round.
On 10 February, after Israeli forces withdrew from the area, the bodies were finally recovered. The family car was riddled with bullets. The ambulance lay burned out nearby.
Subscribe now

## The denial unravelled
Now consider what the Israeli authorities said after these killings.
Initially, the IDF said it was “unfamiliar with the incident described” and was “still looking into it”.
As the case attracted far more international attention than the vast majority of Palestinians killed in Gaza, the Israeli army issued a categorical denial on 24 February.
The IDF Spokesperson’s Unit told the Times of Israel that its preliminary investigation found IDF troops “were not present near the vehicle or within firing range”.
Because Israeli forces supposedly were not there, it also claimed there had been no need for the ambulance to coordinate its movement with the IDF.
Both claims swiftly disintegrated.
Weeks later, an official from COGAT – the Israeli agency responsible for coordinating civilian affairs in the occupied Palestinian territories – told the Washington Post that COGAT had “coordinated everything … including the ambulance that wanted to go and find Hind”, while saying he did not know the specifics.
COGAT then failed to clarify the contradicting accounts when repeatedly asked, while the IDF continued to deny that coordination had taken place.
Then on 16 April, US State Department spokesman Matthew Miller said the Israelis had told Washington that IDF units had, in fact, been in the area – while maintaining they had no knowledge of or involvement in the attack.
So the story had moved from: our troops weren’t there to our troops were there, but they weren’t involved.
Yet the IDF subsequently continued publicly standing by its original denial.
By October 2025, another explanation had emerged: the Israeli government argued that the hundreds of bullet impacts on the car were the product of a firefight between Israeli forces and Palestinian militants.
Then, on 6 April 2026, a website called FactSignal promoted the possibility that Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad had been fighting in the area, suggesting that the family might have been struck in crossfire or by Palestinian mortar or small-arms fire.
This was not simply some random pro-Israel website. At the bottom of the page is this disclosure:

> “This material is distributed by Clock Tower X LLC on behalf of the State of Israel.”
In other words, this material formed part of a propaganda operation conducted on behalf of the Israeli state.
That story has now been abandoned too.
Israel’s latest account accepts that its troops did fire on the family car, but says it was travelling contrary to an evacuation route previously announced to residents.
Just look at the progression:
Israeli troops were not there.
Then: Israeli troops were there, but did not attack the car.
Then: perhaps the damage came from crossfire involving Palestinian fighters.
Now: Israeli troops did fire on the car.
Subscribe now

## The evidence was already there
Here is why the original Israeli denial should never have been treated so credulously.
During Layan’s final conversation with the Red Crescent, she told the dispatcher:

> “They are shooting at us. The tank is next to us.”
The only military operating tanks in Gaza was Israel.
After Layan was killed, Hind herself repeatedly told Red Crescent dispatchers that tanks were around the car and moving closer.
To dismiss those accounts required dismissing what two terrified children reported about the murder of their family - which they had witnessed, and only temporarily survived.
Hind’s mother, Wissam, also said she witnessed fire directed at the vehicle:

> “We saw them when they fired at the car but we didn’t believe they had targeted them, or we didn’t want to believe it.”
There were important investigations by two Western media organisations. But they not only lacked prominence, they remained isolated pieces of reporting rather than changing the wider way the story was framed - and these stories were largely ignored by other media outlets. This is typical of the reporting of the genocide.
The Washington Post had the audio independently analysed. Audio specialists identified at least 62 gunshots in six seconds, in two bursts. An acoustic specialist found that the rate of fire was faster than the sort of rifle Hamas fighters used, and was more consistent with “weapons commonly issued to Israeli forces”.
Then there was the satellite evidence.
The team at Planet Labs supplied the evidence, and a specialist reviewed it on on behalf of the Washington Post. They found at least four Israeli armoured vehicles around 300 metres further along the road from the family car at 3.31pm on 29 January, roughly an hour after Layan’s final call.
More than a dozen additional Israeli armoured vehicles were visible within a quarter of a mile.
Sky News conducted its own analysis and found at least 15 Israeli military vehicles in the area, with the closest roughly 300 metres from the car.
And note this. On 10 February, the IDF itself published a press release stating that “over the last two weeks” its troops had been conducting raids in Shati and Tel al-Hawa – the neighbourhood where Hind and her family were killed.
That press release was later deleted.
Sky News also geolocated footage released by the IDF to show three Israeli units operating less than 650 metres from the car.
The evidence contradicted the categorical Israeli claim that its forces were nowhere close enough to have fired on the family.
A weapons expert from intelligence agency Janes consulted by the Washington Post examined images of the car and concluded that its bullet holes were probably produced by a 7.62-calibre machine gun. They noted that Merkava tanks, Namer armoured personnel carriers and Puma engineering vehicles used by Israel all carry weapons of that calibre.
Then there is Forensic Architecture, the research agency based at Goldsmiths, University of London. Its reconstruction identified 335 projectile impacts on the car and concluded, using the bullet trajectories and acoustic evidence, that the firing came from close range. Its analysis found that whoever was firing would likely have been aware that children were inside.
Remember: this happened in broad daylight.
Subscribe now

## The ambulance – and what the UN found
The ambulance presents another devastating contradiction.
The IDF had argued that the Red Crescent could not have needed Israeli permission to approach Hind because Israeli troops were supposedly absent. But we know that is a lie. Israeli troops were present.
The Washington Post reviewed the COGAT route map transmitted to the Palestinian health liaison, who said permission had been granted. A COGAT official independently confirmed that the ambulance had been coordinated.
The Red Crescent recordings also capture Wissam asking whether access had been coordinated and was safe. The dispatcher confirms that it had, saying they had spent around three hours arranging it.
The ambulance was subsequently found burned out around 50 metres from the family car. Munitions experts who reviewed the damage found it consistent with a large direct-fire projectile of approximately the size of a tank round.
Then came the international investigations.
In October 2024, the UN-mandated Independent International Commission of Inquiry found that the IDF’s 162nd Division had been operating in the area and attributed the deaths of the seven family members and the shelling of the ambulance to Israeli forces. It concluded that the killings amounted to the war crimes of “wilful killing” and “attacking a civilian object”.
In June 2026, the Commission went further. It found that the 401st Brigade of the 162nd Division deliberately fired on the car from close range in the full knowledge that children were inside. They held the same brigade responsible for the shelling of the ambulance.
The commander of the 401st Armoured Brigade at the time was Colonel Beni Aharon. Above him in the chain of command, the 162nd Division was commanded by Brigadier General Itzik Cohen.
Subscribe now

## This pattern did not begin with Hind Rajab
There are many examples of Israeli authorities denying responsibility for crimes, only for the original account to collapse later.
During Israel’s 2008-09 assault on Gaza, Operation Cast Lead, Israel initially denied using white phosphorus. It later acknowledged its use.
In May 2022, Palestinian-American Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh was shot dead in Jenin. Senior Israeli officials initially suggested Palestinian gunmen were responsible. Months later, the IDF acknowledged there was a “high possibility” that she had been accidentally hit by Israeli gunfire.
In August of that year, five Palestinian boys were killed beside a cemetery in Gaza. Israeli officials initially attributed their deaths to a failed Palestinian Islamic Jihad rocket. An Israeli military investigation subsequently concluded that an Israeli air strike had killed them.
You can see the recurring pattern: an immediate dismissal of responsibility, evidence accumulating against it, and - as attention has moved on - a later admission that moves much closer to what witnesses and independent investigators had said from the beginning.
Subscribe now

## What does an Israeli investigation actually mean?
Which brings us back to the newly announced Israeli investigation into Hind’s killing – and the separate investigation into the killing of 15 Palestinians in Tel al-Sultan.
The latter case is itself indicative.
Israeli troops opened fire on emergency vehicles in March 2025. The IDF initially claimed that the vehicles had been “advancing suspiciously” in darkness without headlights or emergency lights.
Video subsequently recovered from the phone of one of the dead paramedics showed the emergency vehicles moving slowly, visibly marked, with their emergency lights flashing.
Israel then withdrew key elements of its original account.
So what reason is there to believe that these newly announced investigations will produce accountability?
According to Israeli human rights organisation Yesh Din, 219 Palestinian fatalities in the occupied West Bank were brought to the military’s attention between 2018 and 2022.
Only one of those 219 fatalities resulted in a prosecution – a rate of 0.4%.
As Yesh Din concluded:

> “The data shows that Israel is unwilling to conduct genuine investigation and prosecution procedures in cases of offenses committed by soldiers.”
And consider what that solitary prosecution actually amounted to.
In March 2019, an Israeli soldier shot dead 23-year-old Palestinian Ahmad Jamal Manasrah near Bethlehem. Earlier, the same soldier had opened fire on Alaa Ghiyada after falsely accusing him of throwing stones. Ghiyada was seriously wounded. Manasrah was killed when he stopped to help him..
The soldier was ultimately convicted of the military-law equivalent of negligent homicide
His punishment?
Three months of unpaid military service, probation and demotion to private. No imprisonment.
He was not prosecuted at all for shooting and seriously wounding Ghiyada.
What about Israel’s record during its genocide in Gaza?
A 2025 investigation by Action on Armed Violence identified 52 publicly reported cases in which the Israeli military said it had conducted or would conduct an investigation into alleged wrongdoing between October 2023 and June 2025.
Of those 52 cases, 46 – 88% – had either been closed with no finding of fault or remained ‘unresolved’ with no reported outcome.
Among the ‘unresolved’ cases was the killing of at least 112 Palestinians waiting for flour in Gaza City in February 2024.
In AOAV’s 52-case sample, just one case had resulted in a prison sentence.
That involved a reservist at the Sde Teiman detention centre who repeatedly attacked bound and blindfolded Palestinian detainees. He was sentenced to seven months in prison and demoted.
Against the scale of death and destruction in Gaza, the fact that this was the sole custodial sentence identified in that sample is extraordinary.
And the contrast with trivial disciplinary offences is striking.
In March 2024, two Israeli soldiers were sentenced to 20 days in a military prison - because they warmed up hot dogs in a military kitchen on Shabbat.
In April 2026, four Border Police officers were sentenced to two weeks in a military prison - because they barbecued on a base, “harming religion and Judaism”.
In May 2026, an Israeli soldier was sentenced to 30 days in military prison for wearing an unauthorised Velcro patch bearing the word “Messiah” on his uniform.
These are the sorts of offences Israeli soldiers are imprisoned for - rather than the mass slaughter of civilians.
Subscribe now

## Then there is World Central Kitchen
The decision over the World Central Kitchen killings is revealing for another reason.
Seven aid workers were killed on 1 April 2024. They did not die in a single strike.
An Israeli drone first hit one WCK vehicle. Two people survived and made it into a second car. Around two minutes later, that vehicle was attacked too. Again, two people survived long enough to reach the third vehicle.
Then Israel struck that one as well.
All seven were killed.
And consider what Israeli forces knew while this was happening.
The WCK mission had been extensively coordinated in advance with the Israeli authorities: the organisation had given them detailed information about the operation, its vehicles, its personnel and the route they intended to take.
There had been armed locally contracted security personnel associated with the convoy, and a man had earlier been seen firing into the air. But by the time the WCK vehicles left the warehouse, those suspected gunmen were travelling in a different direction.
Their vehicle went north. The three WCK cars headed west, towards the coast.
This was not something Israeli surveillance had lost sight of. A UAV followed the security vehicle north and continued watching the suspected gunmen.
Nevertheless, an Israeli operator claimed that a WCK driver appeared to be putting a gun into one of the aid organisation’s vehicles. This was false – something Israel’s own investigation later acknowledged.
The WCK cars were attacked anyway.
An independent Australian government review later found that the attacks on the second and third vehicles breached the IDF’s own Standard Operating Procedures and Rules of Engagement. The strikes also took place within an area Israel had designated a “humanitarian fire control zone”.
Why would Israel deliberately attack the World Central Kitchen?
Consider this. A senior brigade-level officer involved in the operation had previously signed a letter calling for restrictions on aid entering Gaza.
The consequences extended far beyond the seven people killed. Humanitarian organisations suspended operations in Gaza in the aftermath.
Yet Israel has now decided that the conduct of those responsible does not even raise a “reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct”.
There won’t even be a sham investigation.
World Central Kitchen has condemned that decision.

-
- Subscribe now

## This is what impunity looks like
The Israeli military lied and lied about the killing of Hind Rajab and her family.
This has been their modus operandi both before and during the genocide.
They are now using the case for cynical propaganda ends to undermine justice. There will be no accountability for those who perpetrated this crime.
The UN-mandated Commission of Inquiry has correctly concluded that the 401st Brigade deliberately targeted the family car while knowing that children were inside.
These murders cannot be separated from the wider destruction of Palestinian childhood in Gaza.
The same UN Commission reported in June that more than 20,000 Palestinian children had been killed between October 2023 and October 2025. It concluded that “Palestinian children have been deliberately targeted and killed by the Israeli security forces”, and that this formed a key part of the evidence establishing genocidal intent.
These are the most heinous of crimes - facilitated by Western governments and media outlets. It is our responsibility to fight for truth - and justice.

reads.title: IMPORTANT: Unusual Whales and Siebert Financial Announce Strategic Partnership to Launch New Series of ETFs
reads.subtitle: The partnership combines Unusual Whales’ access to political trading activity, shadow data, and unique market intelligence with Siebert’s financial infrastructure and expertise
reads.body:
The partnership brings together two distinct strengths:

- Unusual Whales provides access to a different layer of market intelligence, including political trading disclosures, options activity, market flows and other forms of “shadow data” that can reveal activity and trends beyond traditional financial research; as well as a highly engaged follower base across social media, newsletters and exclusive chats, with more than 5 million followers on X/Twitter alone.

- Siebert provides the financial expertise, infrastructure, and market relationships needed to develop investment products and bring them to investors, thanks also to its circa $19 billion in Assets Under Management and more than 176,000 retail customer accounts.

Together, the companies intend to transform these insights into ETF strategies that give investors new ways to participate in themes and market activity that have historically been difficult to identify or access through traditional investment products.
“We are incredibly excited about what we can build with Unusual Whales,” said John J. Gebbia, CEO of Siebert Financial. “They have built a powerful window into parts of the market that investors increasingly want to understand, from political trading activity to signals that often sit outside traditional research. Siebert brings a solid financial infrastructure, 59 years of experience, and execution capabilities to turn those insights into real investment products. We believe the ETFs coming from this partnership can be unlike anything currently available to investors.”
Unusual Whales has built a large following by making complex and often hard-to-find market information easier for investors to access and understand. Its platform tracks areas including congressional and political trading disclosures, unusual options activity, institutional flows and other market signals that can provide a different perspective on where capital is moving.
“We built Unusual Whales around a simple idea: retail investors shouldn’t be the last ones to know what’s happening in the market. If politicians are trading, potential insiders are placing large bets, or unusual options activity is bubbling up beneath the surface, regular people deserve the tools to see it too,” said Matt Saincome, CEO of Unusual Whales. “This partnership with Siebert allows us to take insights pulled from our tools, data, and worldview and package them into more easily accessible ETFs with a partner who knows how to build, launch, and scale financial products at scale.”

The collaboration is designed to bridge the gap between market intelligence and investable products. The partnership also reflects Siebert’s broader strategy of combining its established financial infrastructure with emerging technology, data and new forms of market access.
Additional information regarding individual ETF strategies, regulatory filings and anticipated launch dates will be announced separately.

reads.title: U.S.-Registered Drone Detected at Site of Suspected CIA Boat Strike
reads.subtitle: A drone registered to U.S. defense contractor Shield AI flew within 500 meters of Ecuadorian fishing boat hours after attack, according to flight data.
reads.body:
As a reader-funded independent news outlet, we operate free from the influence of governments, advertisers, and corporate backers. This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary support of our community of readers. Please consider making a tax-deductible donation to support our work today.
Subscribe now

-
- An eyewitness watches the Negra Francisca boat burning on March 17, 2026 near the Galapagos Islands. Photo: Darwin Flores-Pico.QUITO, Ecuador—In the hours after a mysterious attack on an Ecuadorian fishing boat near the Galápagos Islands on March 17, a drone registered to U.S. defense contractor Shield AI was hovering just 500 meters from the burning vessel, La Negra Francisca, according to a review of flight tracking data by Drop Site News. This represents the first known vehicle to arrive at the site of the strike.
The unattributed bombing of three Ecuadorian fishing boats in January and March, and the subsequent abduction and torture of 36 fishermen, was first reported by Drop Site in April. Last week, The Washington Post, building on Drop Site’s ongoing investigation, reported that the attacks were part of a covert CIA operation.
According to flight and vessel tracking data from Radar 24 and Global Fishing Watch, the drone was a V-BAT model, primarily used for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, but capable of carrying a weapons payload and switching its signal on and off to avoid detection.
The Shield AI drone matches the fishermen’s descriptions of the drones that circled their boats before the bombing, and bears the same red and green lights eyewitnesses reported seeing as they photographed the explosion.
Shield AI did not respond to a request for comment.
The CEO of Shield AI, Brandon Tseng, has publicly stated that the U.S. Coast Guard and Navy are using V-BAT drones “to interdict and destroy billions of dollars’ worth of drugs that were headed for the United States of America.” In 2024, the U.S. Coast Guard signed a $198 million contract with Shield AI for V-BAT drones; in April 2026, Shield AI announced it had received an $800 million contract for V-BAT drones from the U.S. Navy.
No drugs were found on any of the three fishing boats investigated by Drop Site—the Negra Francisca, Don Maca, and Fiorella—all of which were searched and cleared by Ecuadorian coast guard personnel prior to the strikes.
Last month, Drop Site published NASA thermal imagery consistent with an explosion at coordinates 1.5822°N, 87.6958W°, recorded at 1:02 p.m., the time fishermen say they were hit, and in the location where their transponder stopped broadcasting.
Tracking data suggests that the drone launched from a nearby boat on March 17, seven hours after the strike on La Negra Francisca and then circled near the site, its signal disappearing and reappearing. Ascending and descending patterns of movement indicate that the drone may have been landing on a boat and then resuming its flights.
Drop Site previously reported that vessel tracking data showed a U.S. Coast Guard cutter leaving a Galápagos military base a day before the Negra Francisca bombing—despite claiming it only deployed the cutter as a post-incident rescue effort. The Coast Guard vessel’s signal went dark and later appeared in Central American waters 24 hours before the fishermen were placed in El Salvador’s custody.
Video recordings, taken by eyewitnesses to the bombing, show the U.S. Coast Guard patrolling in the aftermath of the airstrike. Drop Site asked the U.S. Coast Guard in June to account for the cutter’s movements after its signal went dark. The Coast Guard responded that it “does not disclose cutter movements during law enforcement missions for operational security.”
In June, the U.S. Coast Guard told The Guardian it deployed its Bertholf cutter for a search-and-rescue operation after receiving a Mayday alert, contradicting prior statements by the U.S. Southern Command, which oversees maritime operations in the Pacific, that it had no knowledge of any U.S. involvement in the incidents. To date, the U.S. Coast Guard has not acknowledged using drones in its purported rescue efforts.
The U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Southern Command, and the Central Intelligence Agency did not respond to questions for this article.
While flight tracking data is recorded in UTC, dating the drone activity as March 18, in Galápagos time (UTC-06:00) both the strike and the subsequent drone activity occurred on March 17.

-
- Graphic: Tomi McCluskeyShield AI, a San Diego-based defense contractor, builds fighter jets and drones powered and piloted by artificial intelligence. The company was founded in 2016 with $1 million in seed funding from the Pentagon’s Defense Innovation Unit and the Naval Special Warfare Command. The Israeli military has reportedly used the company’s self-piloting drones for close quarters combat. V-BAT drones are also used by the Ukrainian military to identify Russian targets, as part of larger drone strike operations.

## Video of the burning fishing boat La Negra Francisca, taken by Darwin Flores-Pico, after the March 17, 2026 attack.

Last week, the New York Times and the Washington Post corroborated much of Drop Site’s original investigation of the attacks. In addition, the Times reported that a patrol plane flew from a military base in El Salvador in the direction of the three boats prior to each of the attacks. The Post identified that plane as FENIX 701, a Cessna business jet equipped with surveillance equipment operating out of Ilopango International Airport, which served as a hub for CIA operations during the Contra War against the Sandinista government of Nicaragua. The plane is registered to a company with virtually no digital footprint that lists its address as a mailbox inside a Virginia UPS store.
The FENIX 701 stopped broadcasting its signal well before reaching any of the boats and returned to base hours before the actual strikes, according to flight data.
The fishermen, like the airplane, eventually wound up in El Salvador. As Drop Site previously reported, men from the Negra Francisca and Don Maca boats were taken hostage by “gringo” gunmen in U.S. military uniforms who they say hooded, handcuffed, and starved them for eight days aboard their U.S.-flagged ship before turning them over to El Salvador’s navy hundreds of miles away from home.

-
- Graphic: Tomi McCluskeySince September 2025, the U.S. military has carried out over 66 strikes on vessels in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific, killing at least 221, as part of Operation Southern Spear. The Trump administration has been boastful and unapologetic about this extrajudicial killing spree, which raises the question of why it would also run a covert CIA operation alongside it, as the Washington Post reported. There is precedent for such parallel operations, however. In April, for example, it was revealed that CIA agents were secretly working joint counter-narcotics raids with local agents in Mexico’s Chihuahua state without informing President Claudia Sheinbaum—despite her administration’s bilateral efforts with U.S. forces.
“We certainly do have cases in which one part of the U.S. government is doing something covertly while another part is doing something overtly,” Vincent Bevins, author of “The Jakarta Method,” a historical examination of the CIA’s Cold War operations, and editor of North South Notes, told Drop Site.
“That covert operation might be doing the same thing in a different way. It might be doing something similar and related,” Bevins added. “Even, at cross purposes, to some extent, with the official government line or official government policy….There are also cases where the only explanation is institutional chaos or poor planning.”

## A Community Under Siege
In June, Alexandra Bravo, a prosecutor investigating the U.S. strikes, was shot dead in the coastal city of Manta, the home port of the three fishing boats. U.S. troops have been deployed in Manta since December 2025, and the return of a de facto U.S. military base there—originally outlawed by the 2007 constitution and again ratified by 60% of Ecuadorian voters last November—evokes painful memories for residents who have not forgotten why it was banned in the first place: the U.S. publicly and brazenly sinking fishing ships off the coast of Manta.
Ecuador is under its 23rd martial law decree, which allows authorities to raid homes and wiretap communications without a warrant, and grants diplomatic immunity to all U.S. forces. President Daniel Noboa justifies the stripping of civil liberties as a necessary part of his “war on narcos.”
The strikes and subsequent abductions left Jordi Flores, a young crewmember aboard the Negra Francisca, with a severe foot injury and unable to work. Erik Coello, a crewmember aboard the Don Maca, which was also struck in March, suffers from 70% vision loss. And the families of the Fiorella, which vanished in January, have been crushed by grief for their missing sons, husbands, and fathers.

-
- Photo of Jordi Flores’ foot injury from the March 17 attack on the fishing boat La Negra Franscisca. Photo: Hernán Flores.Maria Mero, whose husband Gabriel Aladino Mero Delgado and brother Jefferson Ariel Mero Cueva both disappeared on the Fiorella, told Drop Site that her mother-in-law died awaiting her son’s return, falling into a deep depression and ceasing to eat in the weeks leading up to her death. Maria’s young daughter was hospitalized from the anxiety of going seven months without seeing her father. Gabriel’s disappearance also left a void in the family’s finances. Without him, Maria said, the ordinary necessities of life—groceries, her electricity bill, their daughter’s school uniform—are completely unaffordable.
“If the CIA or the United States or the El Salvador patrol or the president is reading this,” Maria said, “please, I beg you, return my husband, my brother, and all the people who are with them.”

reads.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill 17 Palestinians; Tuesday’s primary results; Liberia to take 1,200 deportees from the U.S.
reads.subtitle: Drop Site Daily: August 19, 2026
reads.body:
- Palestinians carry the body of a person killed in an Israeli airstrike on August 19, 2026 in Gaza City, Gaza. Photo by Ahmad Hasaballah/Getty Images.Wednesday, August 19, 2026 – Israel escalates its attacks on Gaza, killing 17, wounding 38 over the past 24 hours. Palestinian child dies of malnutrition in Gaza. Nearly 470 attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank in a week. Land seizures, settler attacks and detentions reported across the occupied West Bank. UN: Gaza remains world’s deadliest place for aid workers in 2025 for third consecutive year. Israel announces probe into two high-profile Gaza massacres. United Arab Emirates halts all trade with Iran after accusing it of launching missiles. President Donald Trump calls Hormuz “New U.S. Territory.” Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf visits Iraq, lauds “resistance.” Pentagon considering Gulf drawdown. Vessel struck, “completely” disabled off of Mokha. Missile strikes in Yemen kill three, including a child, in Hodeidah. Israeli forces continue military activity, demolitions in southern Lebanon despite “ceasefire.” Lebanese army chief: Israel keeps attacking even as army implements agreement. Hezbollah MP: Resistance will confront any Israeli move on Ali Al-Taher. Primary results from Florida, Alaska, Wyoming, and California. Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon criticizes party leadership. Trump pauses new 50% Canada tariffs for three days, cites pending trade deal. Whistleblower alleges Trump antisemitism task force pressured universities despite lacking evidence. U.S. quietly deporting Mexican migrants to Guatemala, Honduras instead of Mexico. Minnesota Attorney General sues Texas Governor Abbott over refusal to extradite ICE agent. Trump administration moves to repeal Clinton-era “roadless rule.” Liberia agrees to take up to 1,200 U.S. deportees over the next year. Trump administration issues more International Criminal Court sanctions. Bolivia arrests major Trump-linked right-wing operative over shooting of activist. Half of Venezuela’s oil is being exported to the U.S. Pakistan will challenge Imran Khan ruling. Israel says strike on Syria intended to block Turkish military buildup. Zelenskyy fires senior aide amid corruption probe. Liberia agrees to accept up to 1,200 U.S. deportees. Iraqi resistance leader decries U.S. control over Iraq’s oil money and airspace. South Korea says Trump military drill cuts may be pressure on Seoul over Iran war, investment.
This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday – Friday

## Palestine

- Israel escalates its attacks on Gaza, killing 17, wounding 38 over the past 24 hours:

- An Israeli strike on a seaside cafe on Tuesday killed seven Palestinians and wounded 14, with Al Jazeera confirming at least one child was among those killed.

- “We don’t know what we’re supposed to deal with anymore. Do we deal with the Israelis? Or the sun burning us inside the tents? Or the water—waking up at 6 a.m. to go get water? Or do we deal with the winter that is still coming, when we’ll also suffer from the weather?” Eyewitness Abu Ahmed said.

- Drop Site’s Mohamed Ahmed submitted video reports from the scene of the port attack, available here and here.

- At least nine Palestinians were killed and 15 wounded on Wednesday in an Israeli airstrike on the Municipalities Police headquarters in Gaza City, according to Gaza’s Interior Ministry. The strike hit during a busy time in the middle of day and close to a crowded municipal park.

- Footage from Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed of the police building attack shows ambulances arriving as people rush to carry the dead and wounded, including a woman and a child.

- “Every day we say, ‘Tomorrow there’s hope. There is still hope,’ while the number of martyrs keeps rising. Let people feel for us. Yesterday, it was the port. Today, the municipal park, full of children. Every day, they take revenge on us,” eyewitness Abu Al-Baha said.

- Separately, an earlier Israeli strike on a motorcycle in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza killed one Palestinian.

- Gaza’s Interior Ministry said Israeli attacks on the civil police force are meant to cripple the police and “spread chaos within Palestinian society.

- Hamas rejected the Israeli military’s claim that resistance leaders were targeted as “baseless.” The group said the attack, coming after recent meetings with mediators and “Board of Peace” member Jared Kushner aimed at advancing the ceasefire agreement, showed Netanyahu’s government was deliberately seeking to undermine those efforts. Hamas called on mediators, particularly the Trump administration, to take immediate action to halt the escalation and pressure Israel to abide by the agreement.

- Palestinian child dies of malnutrition in Gaza: A Palestinian girl died from severe malnutrition on Tuesday as Israel continues to restrict food and other necessities entering Gaza. Since the ceasefire began, Israel has allowed in only 35.3% of the minimum agreed aid deliveries, averaging 211.8 trucks daily against the required 600, a document shared by Palestinian authorities with mediators on Sunday showed.

- The IPC warns that 74,200 children in the Strip require treatment for acute malnutrition through April 2027, including more than 11,400 severe cases. Without sustained aid, nearly 1.9 million Palestinians could face acute food insecurity by December.

- Nearly 470 attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank in a week: Israeli forces and settlers conducted at least 467 attacks against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank in one week, according to the Palestinian prime minister’s office. At least 75 Palestinian homes and structures were also demolished, the office said, calling the attacks “relentless escalation of violence, dispossession, and destruction.”

- Land seizures, settler attacks and detentions reported across the occupied West Bank: Israeli forces detained at least 30 Palestinians in raids across the occupied West Bank between Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning, according to the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society, while Israeli authorities and settlers carried out land seizures, outpost expansion and the continued siege of Palestinian homes. The detainees included journalist Abdulrahman Hassan from Bethlehem, while Israeli forces separately arrested Palestinian Jerusalem Affairs Minister after raiding his home in Silwan.

- Ramallah: Israeli forces shot and critically wounded a Palestinian man during a Tuesday evening raid on Al-Amari refugee camp in Al-Bireh, in the central West Bank, according to the Palestinian Information Center. Israeli authorities declared approximately 1,152 dunams (285 acres) of land in Sinjil, Al-Lubban al-Sharqiya and Qaryut as “state property” to expand the Karmei Oz settlement, the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said.

- Nablus: For a second straight day, Israeli settlers blocked roads in Beit Imrin, northwest of Nablus, isolating families and cutting farmers off from their land, amid a push to build a new settlement outpost nearby. Settlers, backed by Israeli forces, also continued to besiege three Palestinian homes in the Ras Al-Ain area of Qusra for the 11th consecutive day.

- Jenin: Palestinian Ahmed Al-Hatnawi told Radio Al-Shams that Israeli forces etched the number “44” on his forehead and arm after detaining him during a raid in Qabatiyah, Haaretz reported.

- “As if we were animals and beasts,” he said, describing the practice as deliberate humiliation. Al-Hatnawi said Israeli forces took him to a makeshift interrogation site, questioned him for roughly two hours, and threatened him.

- UN: Gaza remains world’s deadliest place for aid workers in 2025 for third consecutive year: Gaza remained the world’s deadliest place for aid workers in 2025 for the third consecutive year, with 186 killed in Israeli attacks despite the ceasefire declared in October, according to the UN humanitarian office (OCHA) in a statement to mark World Humanitarian Day. 68% percent of those killed in Gaza died in aerial bombardments.

- Globally, 350 humanitarian workers were killed in 2025, the second-highest annual toll on record, while 907 aid workers were victims of violence. Sudan recorded a record 71 aid worker deaths.

- Israel announces probe into two high profile Gaza massacres: The Israeli military announced on Wednesday that it would launch criminal investigations into two high profile attacks in Gaza, including the killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab and six members of her family in January 2024, and the massacre of 15 Palestinian aid workers in southern Gaza in March 2025.

- The military said it would not launch criminal investigations into three other attacks that killed aid workers from World Central Kitchen and Doctors Without Borders. The decisions followed reviews by the Israeli military’s fact-finding mechanism, which is officially tasked with examining exceptional operational incidents during wartime.

- In its statement, the Israeli military acknowledged for the first time that it opened fire on the vehicle carrying Hind Rajab and her family after previously denying involvement in the incident and falsely claiming that its forces were not present in the area. Watch an in-depth investigation into the killing of Hind Rajab by Al Jazeera’s Fault Lines in “The Night Won’t End.”

- An investigation by Earshot and Forensic Architecture into the aid worker  massacre found that Israeli soldiers fired nearly a thousand bullets during the attack and that a number of aid workers were executed by Israeli soldiers at point blank range. Read Drop Site’s coverage here.

* An earlier version of today’s Daily said that Palestinian journalist and Drop Site contributor Mohamed Awad had been placed under administrative detention by Israeli authorities based on a post by journalist Mutassem Saqf Al-Hait. This has not been confirmed. Awad’s case has repotedly been referred by military authorities to a legal advisor who will decide next steps in the case. We will update as soon as we have more.

## Iran

- UAE halts all trade with Iran after accusing it of launching missiles: Iranian air defenses detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, the first falling outside its territorial waters and the second within them, the UAE Defense Ministry said on Tuesday, with a phone alert warning residents of a “potential missile threat.” The UAE Foreign Ministry then announced it was halting all trade, commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with Iran until further notice, citing regional escalation.

- Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei “completely rejected” the claim that it launched missiles targeting Emirati territory, calling it damaging to efforts to build regional trust.

- Trump calls Hormuz “New U.S. Territory”: U.S. President Donald Trump posted a map labeling the Strait of Hormuz “NEW U.S. Territory,” and, in a separate post, said no talks with Iran are underway and that the U.S. naval blockade remains “in full force and effect.”

- Trump also claimed Hormuz is “open and operating” and that all naval mines have been removed or detonated.

- Just three transits were recorded on August 16 and 10 crossings on August 17.

- Kpler said vessels continue using Iran’s unilateral routing scheme, with none recorded through the conventional Hormuz traffic-separation system or southern Omani routes yesterday.

- Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tuesday that “until the United States implements its commitments under the memorandum, including lifting the blockade, releasing frozen assets, lifting oil sanctions, ending threats and military operations on all fronts, and the other agreed conditions, the strait will not reopen.”

- Ghalibaf visits Iraq, lauds “resistance”: Ghalibaf arrived in Iraq on Wednesday for a three-day visit.

- Speaking at the site where former General Qassem Soleimani was killed, Ghalibaf said, “Today’s visit to Iraq is aimed at strengthening the new order in the region and accelerating mutual cooperation among all countries of the region, without the intervention of foreign powers.”

- Referring to Iran-backed militias in Iraq, Ghalibaf added, “After years of experience in Iraq, the resistance has gone beyond the borders of the two countries and has become an influential force at the regional and global levels

- Pentagon considering Gulf drawdown: The Pentagon is assessing whether to reduce its Persian Gulf military presence after Iranian strikes exposed the vulnerability of Washington’s regional base network, eight officials told The Washington Post on Tuesday.

- CENTCOM normally stations about 40,000 troops across nearly 20 sites. More than 200 U.S. facilities have been damaged or destroyed since U.S. and Israel launched war; strikes killed six troops in Kuwait and four in Jordan, while U.S. defenses burned through more than 1,000 Patriot and THAAD interceptors.

- Officials have considered shifting forces west toward Jordan, Israel, or Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast.

- Rubio talks with UAE national security official: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke by phone Tuesday with UAE National Security Adviser Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, discussing “regional security issues” including recent developments in Lebanon and the Strait of Hormuz, the State Department said in a statement.

- Rubio continued to call for “freedom of navigation” through the Strait, and urged further U.S.-UAE coordination against Iran and its allies.

## Yemen

- Vessel struck, “completely” disabled off of Mokha: A cargo ship was struck by multiple unidentified projectiles about 40 nautical miles southeast of Mokha, Yemen, resulting in a “complete constructive loss” of the vessel, United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Wednesday.

- The ship was unmanned at the time of the incident, local authorities said.

- Missile strikes kill three, including a child, in Hodeidah: Three civilians, including a child, were killed after two Ansarallah ballistic missiles reportedly struck Al-Khawkhah district in Yemen’s southern Hodeidah province, the Saudi-backed and government-aligned National Resistance Forces said on Wednesday.

## Lebanon

- Israeli forces continue military activity, demolitions in southern Lebanon despite “ceasefire”:

- Israeli warplanes carried out strikes on multiple locations in southern Lebanon early Wednesday, according to Lebanese media. The strikes, according to the Lebanese outlet Al Mayadeen, targeted the important Ali Al-Tahir heights and the area of Kfar Rumman.

- In Nabatieh, two young men were killed and others wounded when a suspicious object believed to be unexploded ordnance left from previous Israeli attacks detonated near the earthen berm between Mayfadoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqieh, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported.

- Israeli forces conducted demolition operations Tuesday evening in Talousseh, Zawtar Sharqieh and Kounin, destroying several homes as attacks continued across southern Lebanon, L’Orient Today reported.

- Forces demolished a water reservoir supplying Mansouri, destroyed two three-story buildings in the village and demolished at least one building.

- Lebanese army chief: Israel keeps attacking even as army implements agreement: The Lebanese military continues carrying out its obligations under the U.S.-brokered framework agreement while Israeli forces continue their “attacks and violations,” Lebanese Army commander Rodolphe Haykal said via NNA.

- Haykal made the remarks during a meeting with Edward Gabriel, president of the American Task Force for Lebanon.

- Hezbollah MP: Resistance will confront any Israeli move on Ali Al-Taher: Hezbollah Member of Parliament Hassan Ezzeddine said the group would not abandon the Ali Al-Taher heights and would “confront any act of aggression” against the strategic position with all available capabilities, speaking to the Russian news outlet Sputnik.

- Israeli forces have been dropping explosives around the heights almost daily, amid reports Israel could be preparing a larger operation there.

- “Ali Al-Taher is one of the resistance’s key positions,” Ezzeddine said, adding that Iranian assistance would provide additional strength. “If assistance comes from Iran, that would be light upon light,” he said. He suggested Iran, which has established deterrence against Israeli strikes on Beirut, may act if Israel acts against the strategic heights.

## U.S. News

- Tuesday’s primary results:

- State Rep. Angie Nixon defeated former Lt. Col. Alex Vindman in the Florida Democratic Senate Primary. Vindman had a significant fundraising advantage over Nixon, having raised $16.3 million to Nixon’s $975,000 before the primary, but Nixon handily defeated him, receiving 56% of the vote in Tuesday night’s primary. DSA-member Nixon will face GOP Sen. Ashley Moody in the November general election. In an interview with CNN following her victory, Nixon said Democratic leaders Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer should face scrutiny as too many “corporate-established Democrats” are beholden to companies rather than ordinary people.

- Rep. Jared Moskowitz defeated his DSA-backed opponent Oliver Larkin in the Democratic primary for Florida’s 23rd congressional district. Moskowitz, one of the Democratic Party’s more ardent supporters of Israel, used the occasion of his primary victory to taunt political streamer Hasan Piker, offering his “condolences” to Piker after the AP called the race.

- Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz won her primary in the redrawn 20th congressional district, defeating four Black opponents in the majority Black district.

- Rep. Byron Donalds easily won the Republican nomination in the Florida gubernatorial primary on Tuesday, and will face Democrat David Jolly in the November election to replace term-limited Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis.

- Republican Rep. Cory Mills, under investigation for sexual misconduct by the House Ethics Committee, lost to Ryan Elijah, a former local TV anchor, in Florida’s 7th district. President Trump had endorsed Mills, making him the second Republican (after Tennessee Rep. Andy Ogles) to lose a primary with the president’s endorsement. Elijah will face Democrat Bale Dalton, a former NASA official, in the November general election.

- Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola holds a tentative, 2-point lead over GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska’s nonpartisan primary. Both are projected to advance to the November general election, in a race that could determine the control of the Senate.

- Progressive state Sen. Aisha Wahab holds a narrow lead over the moderate and AIPAC-backed public transit official Melissa Hernandez in the special primary to replace California Rep. Eric Swalwell. As of Wednesday morning, Wahab leads Hernandez by 2 percentage points, according to NBC News.

- Eric Barlow, a rancher and state senator, defeated the Trump-endorsed public education superintendent Megan Degenfelder in Wyoming’s gubernatorial primary on Tuesday. His victory makes him nearly certain to win the general election in the deep-red state, where voters gave Trump his highest margin of victory in the 2024 presidential election.

- Trump administration moves to repeal Clinton-era “roadless rule”: The U.S. Forest Service advanced a proposal Tuesday to repeal the 2001 “roadless rule,” opening nearly 45 million acres of national forest wilderness to road construction and logging and eliminating protections that have stood for a quarter century, including for nine million undeveloped acres in Alaska’s Tongass National Forest.

- Environmentalists have warned that the move endangers drinking water supplies and wildlife habitats, and ecologists told the New York Times that new roads could increase wildfire risk by bringing more human activity into previously undisturbed areas.

- The proposal, expected to be published in the Federal Register this week before a public comment period, follows Trump’s push for a 25% increase in national forest logging and Rollins’ prior declaration of an “emergency situation,” which allowed the Forest Service to fast-track timber production by curtailing environmental review.

- Trump pauses new 50% Canada tariffs for three days, cites pending trade deal: President Donald Trump said Tuesday night he was pausing the 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days, saying on Truth Social that the U.S. and Canada “have a DEAL!” pending finalization, following talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. The tariffs, which had been set to take effect early Wednesday under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, targeted goods including alcohol, hockey equipment, cement, and dairy products.

- Whistleblower alleges Trump antisemitism task force pressured universities despite lacking evidence: A whistleblower complaint from former DOJ civil rights attorney Haley Van Erem, made public by Rep. Jamie Raskin on Tuesday, alleges the Trump administration’s antisemitism task force pursued “predetermined” outcomes against Harvard, Brown, and Columbia despite little evidence supporting systemic Title VI violations, overruling career attorneys who objected to the investigations.

- U.S. quietly deporting Mexican migrants to Guatemala, Honduras instead of Mexico: The Trump administration has been sending deportees from Mexico to Guatemala and Honduras rather than back to Mexico, despite Mexico’s willingness to accept all its citizens, according to two Department of Homeland Security officials who spoke to CBS News on Tuesday.

- Minnesota AG sues Texas Gov. Abbott over refusal to extradite ICE agent: Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison sued Texas Gov. Greg Abbott on Tuesday to compel the extradition of ICE agent Christian Castro, who faces Minnesota charges of assault and falsely reporting a crime in connection with the January shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis.

- Ellison warned Castro could be released from Texas custody as soon as August 26 under a 90-day detention limit and potentially flee to Mexico, where the lawsuit says he has discussed marrying a woman and buying a house.
📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill?  Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com

## Other International News

- Trump administration issues more ICC sanctions: The Trump administration sanctioned International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye on Tuesday as the court pursues investigations into Israel’s crimes in Gaza and the West Bank.

- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu celebrated the move on X, called the ICC a “kangaroo court” and praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio for making its officials “face consequences.” Rubio says his campaign aims to “dismantle” the court.

- Washington has sanctioned at least 11 ICC officials, including prosecutor Karim Khan, who secured arrest warrants for Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant on charges of committing war crimes in Gaza.

- Bolivia arrests major Trump-linked right-wing operative over shooting of activist: Bolivian police have arrested Fernando Cerimedo, an Argentine political operative with connections to President Donald Trump’s former campaign manager, as the main suspect in the shooting of his former partner, lawyer and activist Nadia Beller.

- Beller, 33, was shot three times outside a hotel in Santa Cruz de la Sierra on Monday night by two attackers disguised as delivery workers, according to La Nación. She survived and is hospitalized in stable condition.

- Cerimedo was detained early Tuesday at Viru Viru airport trying to board a flight to Buenos Aires. He denies involvement, calling it a “campaign against him.”

- Cerimedo is a business partner of Brad Parscale, Donald Trump’s former campaign manager, in the Buenos Aires consultancy Numen. The firm worked the campaigns of Javier Milei in Argentina, Rodrigo Paz in Bolivia, and Nasry Asfura in Honduras, all right-wing victories.

- Half of Venezuela’s oil is being exported to the U.S.: About half of Venezuela’s oil production is now being exported to the United States, Kyle Haustveit, an undersecretary in the U.S. Department of Energy, said Tuesday.

- “In the last couple of months, we’re seeing north of 500,000 barrels, or approximately half of the production coming out of Venezuela, coming to the United States…to the refineries that were built specifically for that crude,” Haustveit told an industry event in Houston.

- The surge marks a sharp redirection of Venezuela’s oil away from China, its longtime top buyer, toward the U.S. At the end of 2025, only about 135,000 of Venezuela’s roughly 1 million barrels per day went to American refineries.

- Pakistan will challenge Imran Khan ruling: Pakistan’s government said on Wednesday it would challenge a Supreme Court order requiring jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be transferred within two days to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad and given access to his personal physician.

- Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said the ruling was “not within four walls of the law,” arguing that convicted prisoners must be treated in jail or at a public hospital. The government will seek a review and modification of the order, according to AFP.

- Khan, 73, has been jailed in Rawalpindi since August 2023. His lawyers say he has lost significant vision in his right eye. His PTI party welcomed the order and demanded it be implemented immediately.

- Israel says strike on Syria intended to block Turkish military buildup: Israel said its eight strikes on Syria’s Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib province were intended to prevent a Turkish military deployment, according to Axios and the Israeli prime minister’s office.

- The attacks damaged the runway and storage facilities, with no casualties reported, according to regional media.

- Israel’s Prime Minister’s Office claimed Syria was about to breach a “status quo” security agreement by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at the base.

- A Turkish official denied any Turkish presence there, telling Axios: “Israel is inventing pretexts to bomb neighboring countries and destabilize the region.”

- Zelenskyy fires senior aide amid corruption probe: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed deputy presidential office head Iryna Mudra after anti-corruption investigators searched her office in a money-laundering probe.

- The latest scandal follows a series of corruption investigations that have reached officials close to Zelenskyy, including the resignation of his former Chief of Staff Andriy Yermak last year.

- The political crisis widened after recently ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for a mechanism to hold national elections despite martial law, arguing that Ukraine’s political system had become focused on preserving itself and resisting change.

- Liberia agrees to accept up to 1,200 U.S. deportees: Liberia said it will receive as many as 1,200 people deported from the United States who are not Liberian nationals, in one of the largest such arrangements under the Trump administration’s expanded use of third-country removals.

- The transfers are expected to take place over the next year, with an initial group of 20 due to arrive Thursday. Liberian officials said the group will include people from Africa, North and South America, and the Caribbean.

- The deal is part of a broader U.S. policy of deporting migrants to countries other than their own, including people who may have U.S. protection orders barring return to their home countries.

- Iraqi resistance leader decries U.S. control over Iraq’s oil money and airspace: Abu Ala al-Walai, secretary-general of the Iraqi armed group Kataib Sayyed al-Shuhada, denounced U.S. economic and military domination of Iraq in a statement on X on Tuesday.

- “In my country, oil is sold, but Iraq has no right to dispose of its own money because there is an American occupation,” he wrote.

reads.title: Spot Gamma Heatmap - A Breakdown
reads.subtitle: A Primer on Spot Gamma Heatmaps
reads.body:
Spot Gamma Heatmaps: Reading where dealers are positioned
Market makers are the most predictable traders in the market. It’s not because they’re dumb, but rather because they don’t have a choice. When they sell you an option they have to hedge it, and that hedging leaves a footprint on the tape.
The newly released Spot Gamma Heatmap (available with any platform subscription) is a visual of those footprints: every strike and expiry for any underlying, shaded by how badly dealers have to hedge there and which direction that hedging pushes price.
Before we dive into this breakdown just know that there are other methodologies to analyze GEX, and this one ranks among the top.

-
-

## Interpreting the Colors
Every cell in the grid is a strike (rows) at an expiry (columns), shaded along a red to green gradient.

A cell shaded green suggests that dealers are long gamma at that level. Long-gamma dealers hedge against the move. They sell into strength and buy into weakness. That’s a stabilizing force. Green zones are where you get pinning, chop, and ranges that refuse to break.

Red cells suggest that dealers are short gamma at that level. Short-gamma dealers hedge with the move. They buy higher and sell lower, which pours fuel on whatever direction price is already going. Red zones are where volatility expands: gap-and-go, squeezes, and the air pockets that turn a normal day into a spicy one.

That’s the whole intuition. Green = suppressed. Red = amplified.

## How the values are derived
Now you know what the colors mean. Here’s how the values are derived.
GEX represents the dollars needed to hedge against a 1% move in the underlying stock price.
GEX = gamma * 100 * 0.01 * volume * stock price * stock price
VEX measures how hedging changes as implied volatility moves.
VEX = vanna * 100 * 0.01 * volume * stock price * iv
For directionalized GEX, market makers are on the opposite side of the trade. If a trade is closer to the ask, the customer is assumed buying and the market maker is selling, so the value is multiplied by -1.
100 represents the number of shares in one contract.
For GEX, 0.01 represents a 1% move in the stock price.

## The Gamma Flip
A number of importance is the gamma flip, which is the price level where net dealer gamma crosses from positive to negative.

-
- Using the same screenshot as above… on this $AAPL example it’s marked at 290.84.

Above this level dealers are net long gamma across the board, so the market is in a dampening regime: moves get faded, ranges hold, and mean reversion tends to win.
With spot above 306 $AAPL is comfortably above its flip.
Below the flip dealers turn net short and the market moves into an amplifying regime. This is where downside gets disorderly, because the same hedging that used to calm the tape now accelerates it.
The flip is why the character of a stock can change so violently at a specific price.

##
Call Wall and Put Wall: the ceiling and the floor
Two levels get called out explicitly:

The Call Wall is the strike with the largest positive gamma concentration above spot. Big positive-gamma strikes act like magnets that also resist being pierced: price often drifts toward the wall into expiration and then stalls, because dealers are leaning against every push through it. Think of it as a soft ceiling.

The Put Wall is its downside twin - the largest concentration below spot. It tends to act as support, and it’s often the last stop before the gamma flip. Lose the put wall and you’re frequently trading your way toward that amplifying regime, which is why breaks of the put wall often get people’s attention.

##
Putting it together
Find the flip to know the regime; above it, expect dampening; below it, expect fireworks.
Mark the call wall and put wall as your near-term ceiling and floor. Watch whether cells are green (suppression) or red (amplification) around current price.
